q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT X.CLASS FROM (SELECT CLASS, COUNT(STUDENT) FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(STUDENT)>=5) X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.CLASS FROM (SELECT CLASS, COUNT(STUDENT) FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(STUDENT)>=5) X
explanation: Both Q1 and Q2 return the same result. They both select classes from the COURSES table that have at least 5 students. Q1 uses COUNT(*) in the HAVING clause, while Q2 uses COUNT(STUDENT). Since STUDENT is part of the primary key, every row in COURSES has a unique STUDENT, so COUNT(STUDENT) and COUNT(*) are equivalent in this context. The subquery in Q2 is unnecessary and does not change the outcome.
